about: Vajra Yoga | Find Your Inner Light
A devoted practitioner and teacher of Vajra Yoga, dedicated to helping others discover no-harm way to treat their bodies.

My journey with yoga began over 15 years ago during a period of personal transformation. What started as a physical practice quickly became a doorway to profound inner change. Today, I am honored to share this path with students from all walks of life.
My practice is based on these ideas: - Do no harm; - Every person's body and therefore practice is different; - By controlling the body, we control the mind

I think I was blessed to be a student of famous Russian and Ukranian yoga teachers such as A. Pakhomov, E. Trostnitskaya, I. Mezhakova and more. Attended visceral therapy and traumatic protection in yoga various seminars.

My yoga journey began at an Ashtanga yoga school. I was drawn to its strength and challenging nature. Over time, however, my appetite for difficulty and my ego's "no pain, no gain" mentality evolved into a search for wisdom and a deeper understanding of the philosophy behind the practice - and the true purpose of the human body. I learned to distinguish what truly matters in yoga from what doesn't, and that shift in perspective transformed my life.
Completed Vajra Yoga (CAS) Teacher Training course.
Obtained CPR/AED certification for safety in practice.
Completed specialized training in visceral therapy techniques.
Two decades of personal yoga journey

When I am not teaching, you will find me in nature, hiking trails or sitting by water. I am an avid reader of poetry and philosophy, and I believe that wisdom can be found in the most unexpected places.
I would love to meet you on the mat and be part of your journey. Whether you are taking your first yoga class or deepening an established practice, there is a place for you here.

Vajra Yoga International Federation, founded by Anatoliy Pakhomov, is the only certified organization teaching therapeutic spinal care rooted in ancient Yoga principles.
Vajra Yoga is a holistic way of performing asanas (postures) aimed to preserve and improve spinal health.

The term "Vajra" (Tibetan: "Dorje") has several interpretations, including: diamond, lightning bolt, enlightenment, instant enlightenment, primordial state, the immovable state attained through Mahamudra practice. In Vajra Yoga, we understand Vajra to mean the primordial state, also called non-duality.
Shoulders parallel to hips. This fundamental alignment principle protects the spine and ensures safe, effective practice in every posture.
The three essential phases of each practice. We stretch to create space, strengthen to build stability, and relax to integrate and restore.
Synchronize breath with movement; use Kumbhaka (breath hold) techniques. The breath guides each transition and deepens the practice.
Being present here and now. Through mindful awareness, we cultivate the primordial state of non-dual presence in every moment.
Twisting compresses the intervertebral foramina, which can impair nerve function and lead to internal organ dysfunction.
Deep side bends may trigger vertebral shifts that compress nerve roots and cause health issues. Pelvic tilting can also lead to persistent sacroiliac joint displacement.
Deep backbends may cause vertebral misalignment, which can disrupt nerve supply to internal organs and also lead to herniated discs.
In headstands, the thoracic spine experiences increased load from the weight of the legs, pelvis, and large lumbar vertebrae.
